newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein says Mideast peace top priority.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein says Mideast peace top priority.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein has told incoming Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali that the top foreign policy priority is commitment to the Middle East peace process and support for Palestinian calls for statehood.

"The first (point) is our commitment to the peace process and our concern to support it to enable it to overcome all the obstacles that it is exposed to," the king told Majali in his letter of appointment, published by the official Petra news agency.
"And in this context I affirm the continuation of our support to our Palestinian brothers until they attain their rights and set up their state on their land," the king said.
King Hussein appointed Majali on Wednesday to take over from Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti, prime minister since February last year.
The king said Majali's principal job was to prepare Jordan for parliamentary elections, due to be held in November.
"The main task which your government is taking on is the holding of elections," he said, but hinted the government's life could extend beyond the election date.
The king's letter also called for a streamlining Jordan's bloated bureaucracy and "purifying" government bodies of excess or incompetent staff to pave way for more active and capable people.
Majali, 71, was prime minister in 1993 when Jordan held its first multi-party polls since 1957. He also was prime minister when Jordan signed the 1994 peace agreement with Israel.
